proof.text: Put $S=B^{\mathrm{op}}$, $T=E^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $u=p^{\mathrm{op}}:T\to S$. Opposite simplicial sets reverse the ordered vertices, as specified in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Thus a right-horn lifting problem for $p$ becomes a left-horn problem for $u$: the index $i$ becomes $n-i$. In particular $u$ is a left fibration, with no restriction on empty fibers. The strict fibers of $p$ are Kan by [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers]. Write $\mathsf{RFib}(K)$ for the simplicial category of small right fibrations over $K$, with mapping complexes $\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}$. By [lem-coef-cone-straightening-coherent-evaluation], there is an equivalence $\Phi_K:N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathsf{RFib}(K)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$, natural under base pullback and compatible with evaluation on fibers. Apply it with $K=T$ and choose $q:Y\to T$ with $\Phi_T(q)\simeq G$. All total simplicial sets here are $\mathcal U$-small; the categories of such objects are formed in a containing universe.

source.place: Section 2.2.1 and Proposition 2.2.3.11; the coherent-evaluation compatibility is the cited DAG theorem. Opposite horn calculation written explicitly.

proof.text:
Define a simplicial set $R$ over $S$ directly. Its $n$-simplices over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$ are simplicial maps $h:T\times_S\Delta^n\to Y$ over $T$. An operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ sends $(\sigma,h)$ to $(\sigma\alpha,h\circ(\mathrm{id}_T\times\Delta(\alpha)))$. The identity and composition equations follow from those for precomposition, so this defines $r:R\to S$. For any simplicial set $A\to S$, currying gives an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(A,R)\cong\operatorname{Fun}_{/T}(A\times_ST,Y).$$
In degree $m$, a map $A\times\Delta^m\to R$ evaluates to a map $(A\times_ST)\times\Delta^m\to Y$; conversely restrict such a map along each simplex $\Delta^n\to A\times\Delta^m$. These operations are inverse and commute with all operators. Hence $R=\Pi_uY$ is defined without choosing limits. Mapping sets, products and pullbacks use [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Section 4.4, the ordinary pullback/right-adjoint construction; its simplexwise data and currying are written here in full.

proof.text: To fill a right horn $\Lambda_i^n\to R$ over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$, curry its data as in the preceding step. The problem becomes extension of a map $T\times_S\Lambda_i^n\to Y$ over $T$ across $T\times_S\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow T\times_S\Delta^n$. The map $T\times_S\Delta^n\to\Delta^n$ is a left fibration, since its left-horn problems are the corresponding problems for $u$. By [lem-coef-left-fibration-right-anodyne-base-change], the displayed inclusion is right anodyne. A right fibration lifts against every such map: the class of maps with the left lifting property against $q$ contains the generating right horns and isomorphisms and is closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts, exactly the operations in [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. Thus $q$ gives the extension and currying gives the required horn filler. This proves that $r$ is a right fibration, including the $n=1$ horns. Since $S$ is a quasicategory, an inner horn in $R$ is filled by first filling its image in $S$ and then using the inner-fibration part of $r$; hence $R$ is also a quasicategory.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.11 and Proposition 4.4.4(iv); the dependent-product horn argument is written by the second reader from these lifting statements.

proof.text:
Pullback $u^*$ preserves right fibrations by the same lifting-square argument. The preceding construction is a simplicial functor $\Pi_u:\mathsf{RFib}(T)\to\mathsf{RFib}(S)$: a parameterized map $v:Y\times\Delta^m\to Y'$ over $T$ sends $(h,t)$ to $v\circ(h,t)$. It respects composition and identities by evaluation. Currying therefore restricts to an enriched adjunction
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(A,\Pi_uY)\cong\operatorname{Fun}_{/T}(u^*A,Y)$$
for every right fibration $A\to S$. Its counit $u^*\Pi_uY\to Y$ evaluates a section at its argument. Both mapping complexes are Kan by [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. The isomorphism is composition with this evaluation after pullback, since a map $a:A\to\Pi_uY$ evaluates as $(x,t)\mapsto a(x)(t)$; the inverse sends a map $v$ to the section $t\mapsto v(x,t)$. These equalities hold with the additional $\Delta^m$ coordinate, so also for transformations and higher parameters.

source.place: Section 4.4 pullback/right-adjoint construction; explicit enriched currying and evaluation, with Kan mapping complexes from the cited presentation theorem.

proof.text:
The enriched adjunction gives an equivalence on the whole coherent-nerve mapping spaces, not only their components. Here is the comparison explicitly. For a locally Kan simplicial category $\mathcal A$, an $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Map}^R_{N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal A}(a,b)$ is an enriched functor $\mathfrak C[J^n]\to\mathcal A$ with the entire initial face constant at $a$. Its only nonidentity datum is a map $Q^n\to\mathcal A(a,b)$, so this mapping space is $\operatorname{Sing}_Q\mathcal A(a,b)$. The maps $p_{\operatorname{Sing}_Q M}$ and $e_M$ of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution] give a natural weak-equivalence span
$$\operatorname{Sing}_Q M\ \leftarrow\ |\operatorname{Sing}_Q M|_Q\ \to M$$
for Kan $M$. Apply this to the two Kan mapping complexes in the enriched adjunction. Their isomorphism, the comparison span and its degree-zero evaluations are natural, so the resulting equivalence of coherent mapping spaces is the one induced by the evaluation counit. The coherent nerves are quasicategories by [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-quasicategory].

source.place: Section 2.2.2, Corollary 2.2.2.10 and Section 2.2.4; explicit right-pinched mapping-space comparison.

proof.text:
Set $L=\Phi_S(r):B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$. Naturality of $\Phi$ under base pullback identifies $\Phi_T(u^*r)$ with $Lp$; the evaluation counit therefore gives $\eta:Lp\to G$. At $b\in B$, the defining formula for $R$ identifies its strict fiber with
$$R_b=\operatorname{Fun}_{/E_b^{\mathrm{op}}}(E_b^{\mathrm{op}},Y|_{E_b^{\mathrm{op}}}).$$
By [lem-coef-right-fibration-section-limit] this section space, with its evaluation cone, is the limit of the fiber-transport functor on $(E_b^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}=E_b$. By [lem-coef-cone-straightening-coherent-evaluation], that whole transport functor is equivalent to $G_b$, since $\Phi$ commutes with restriction and identifies right-fibration transport with coherent evaluation. The same comparison identifies $L(b)$ with $R_b$ and the fiber restriction of $\eta$ with this evaluation cone. Hence it is a limiting cone on precisely $G_b$. This checks the specified counit, not merely the equivalence class of the limit object.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.3.4, opposite form, and Remark 3.3.3.5; coherent-evaluation and base-pullback compatibility from the cited DAG theorem.

proof.text:
For any $F:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$, use $\Phi_S$ to represent it by $A\to S$. Base-pullback compatibility represents $Fp$ by $u^*A$. Apply the mapping-space equivalence of Step 5 and the functor equivalences $\Phi_S,\Phi_T$ to obtain
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(F,L)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(E,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(Fp,G).$$
Functor equivalences induce mapping-space equivalences by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. By the explicit counit calculation in Steps 4-6, the displayed map is composition with $\eta$. The simplicial functor $\Pi_u$, conjugated by $\Phi_S$ and a coherent inverse of $\Phi_T$, supplies $\operatorname{Ran}_p$ as a coherent functor on all $G$. Currying and evaluation commute with maps in $A,Y$ and all parameter operators; the comparison spans and $\Phi$ are coherent natural comparisons. Thus the equivalence is natural in $F,G$ and retains every higher parameter simplex, as required.

source.place: Dual universal mapping-space conclusion; here deduced from the explicit enriched adjunction rather than the relative-join existence route.

proof.text: If $E_b=\varnothing$, the section formula has exactly one simplex in every degree, so $R_b=\Delta^0$ and the cone of Step 6 is the terminal empty-diagram cone. If $E=\varnothing$, the defining formula gives $R=S$, the terminal right fibration, and $L$ is terminal-valued. If $B=\varnothing$, then $E=\varnothing$ and both diagram categories have the unique empty diagram. If $p$ is the identity, the same formula gives $\Pi_uY=Y$ and the evaluation counit is the identity. In general every degree of $R$ is a union, indexed by the small set $S_n$, of sets of maps between $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets. It is therefore still $\mathcal U$-small. Only the categories of all such objects require a containing universe. No nonemptiness or extra completeness hypothesis was introduced; the construction in fact supplies the required fiber limits in spaces.

source.place: Size convention of Definition 1.2.16.1; empty and identity cases computed directly from the section formula.

proof_origin.place: Second-reader construction: simplexwise dependent product along the opposite left fibration, using Proposition 4.4.11 and existing coherent evaluation and section-limit theorems. The statement is checked against Kerodon 02ZL and 0309. This is not a transcription of their relative-join proof. Online sources read; archival copies WANTED in the report.

title: Pointwise right Kan extension along a right fibration
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functor categories and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the universe $\mathcal U$ of spaces [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $p:E\to B$ be a right fibration of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] between $\mathcal U$-small quasicategories, and let $G:E\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ be a coherent functor. For each $b\in B$, write $E_b$ for the fibre, a Kan complex by [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers], and $G_b:E_b\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ for the restricted diagram. If each $G_b$ has a limit in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$, then there is a coherent functor $\operatorname{Ran}_pG:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ and a counit $\eta:(\operatorname{Ran}_pG)p\to G$ whose component over $b$ is the limiting cone on $G_b$. The pair $(\operatorname{Ran}_pG,\eta)$ is a right Kan extension: for every coherent $F:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$, composition with $\eta$ induces an equivalence of whole mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(F,\operatorname{Ran}_pG)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(E,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(Fp,G)$. These constructions and equivalences are natural in $G,F$ and in simplicial parameters; empty fibres are allowed and functor categories may be formed in a containing universe.
